source: Saracen Bridge Ltd (Jon Chadwick, Director): producer-fee allowance for incentive eligibility
notes: The figures concern eligible expenditure, before applying the rebate or tax-credit rate.
"Confirm" means a reliable numerical maximum could not be established for that route; it should not be treated as uncapped.
Calculate the eligible producer fee first, then express it as a percentage of the worldwide budget.
Where the cap is shared with other ATL costs or overheads, subtract those qualifying costs before calculating the remaining producer-fee allowance.
A contractual EP fee can exceed the eligible amount; the excess simply should not be included in the incentive calculation.
Have the local incentive accountant confirm the selected route and any entries marked "confirm" before locking the finance plan.

routes.allowance: No fixed producer-specific percentage identified for AVEC.
routes.apply: Claim only the qualifying production-related portion. HMRC requires allocation between development and qualifying production phases; a fee covering the whole project is not automatically wholly eligible.

routes.allowance: Normally 10% or 15% of the global budget, shared between producer, co-producer, EP fees and production/corporate overheads.
routes.apply: Revenue normally accepts 15% where eligible expenditure exceeds 80% of the global budget, and 10% where it is below 80%. These are acceptance benchmarks: higher amounts can be substantiated. Exactly 80% needs clarification because the guidance's wording does not resolve that boundary.

routes.allowance: For budgets above €500,000: 5% of production costs excluding the producer fee, capped at €250,000.
routes.apply: Smaller-budget limits are €15,000 for budgets up to €300,000 and €25,000 for budgets above €300,000–€500,000. Exceptions require approval. This is a recognised-cost ceiling; German territorial eligibility still applies.

routes.allowance: 5% of the production costs for which the service producer is responsible, excluding its fee; maximum €350,000.
routes.apply: This concerns the production-service-provider fee, not an unrestricted additional foreign EP fee. Regional funds have separate conditions.

routes.allowance: 4% of the Hungarian budget, pooled across producer fees.
routes.apply: Includes line, co-, executive and other producers. NFI also excludes purchases of goods/services from the foreign producer or co-producer, so a foreign company's fee needs particular scrutiny.

routes.allowance: 0% for producer fees and general company overheads under this route's eligible-cost rules.
routes.apply: The separate 30% overall ATL ceiling does not make producer fees eligible. Domestic production credits and regional grants require separate assessment.

routes.allowance: Shared ATL allowance of €1 million or 30% of total Malta eligible spend, under the applicable approved option.
routes.apply: Shared with directors, cast and stunts; line producers are excluded from this ATL category. Only Malta-attributable work qualifies. The guidelines also cap the rebate generated by ATL expenditure at €5 million. Confirm the option with the Commission before budgeting it.

routes.allowance: Lower of €100,000 or 20% of final actual Malta spend.
routes.apply: This is a separate fee category from the individual producer's ATL remuneration.

routes.regions: National framework, including mainland regions, Balearics and Canaries
routes.allowance: Executive-producer remuneration: 5% of the film's recognised realisation cost under ICAA cost-recognition rules.
routes.apply: Do not automatically apply this as the foreign-production tax-credit allowance. The Article 36.1/36.2 route and the fee's classification must be checked. A higher Canary Islands incentive rate does not itself increase the producer-fee allowance.

routes.allowance: Do not automatically apply the ICAA 5% executive-producer allowance to this route.
routes.apply: The Article 36.1/36.2 route and the fee's classification must be checked. A higher Canary Islands incentive rate does not itself increase the producer-fee allowance.

routes.allowance: Executive-producer remuneration up to the higher of 10% of production cost or €100,000, limited to the actual qualifying fee.
routes.apply: This is specific to that route; it should not be copied automatically into Navarra's foreign-service-production calculation.

routes.allowance: The Article 65.1 allowance should not be copied automatically into this calculation.
routes.apply: Confirm the fee treatment for Navarra's foreign-service-production route.

routes.regions: Basque Country: Bizkaia, Gipuzkoa and Álava
routes.allowance: Confirm separately for each provincial tax route.
routes.apply: No universal producer-fee percentage has been verified across these three regimes.

routes.allowance: Confirm the fee classification; no blanket producer-fee percentage verified.
routes.apply: The rules identify eligible production payroll and services, with territorial and nationality/residency conditions. They do not justify inserting an automatic percentage for a foreign producer's corporate fee.

routes.allowance: No fixed producer-specific percentage verified.
routes.apply: Actual qualifying Czech expenditure must be established. Fundraising activities, certain development costs, unpaid own contributions and remuneration for statutory company-office duties are excluded.

routes.allowance: For non-documentaries, 20% of total film expenditure is the shared ATL/development ceiling in the published guidance checked.
routes.apply: Producers share this allowance with other covered ATL expenditure. Documentaries are exempt from this cap. The announced removal should not be assumed effective without checking the applicable enacted rules.

routes.allowance: No fixed individual EP percentage identified. Corporate production-company/service fees are excluded as such.
routes.apply: An individual EP's actual services in Australia may qualify where they concern making the film. Fees solely for financing or distribution are excluded. Separately identifiable qualifying services can be assessed individually.

routes.regions: State and territory grants and top-ups
routes.allowance: Confirm against the particular programme and approved budget.
routes.apply: The federal Producer Offset's 20% figure is not a universal producer-fee allowance for every state grant.

routes.allowance: Former 20% ATL cap removed for productions starting principal photography/eligible PDV from 1 January 2026.
routes.apply: This permits assessment of actual eligible expenditure, not an arbitrary budget percentage. Non-resident non-cast personnel must generally work in New Zealand for at least 14 days in aggregate.

routes.allowance: The federal CRA's 10% × actual B+C producer-fee reference applies to specified related-party, ownership and financier-associated fees. CRA expressly says it is not a maximum.
routes.apply: Higher fees can be justified; arm's-length contractual fees are assessed differently. Provincial eligibility remains a separate calculation. B+C means production plus post-production costs, excluding the ATL and other budget sections.

routes.regions: British Columbia: Vancouver, regional BC and Vancouver Island
routes.allowance: BC expressly refers applicants to the CRA producer-fee policy.
routes.apply: Apply the qualifying BC labour rules; 10% of B+C is not a hard provincial budget cap.

routes.regions: Ontario: GTA, regional and northern Ontario
routes.allowance: Use the federal benchmark where applicable, but confirm the provincial fee allowance and labour/service allocation under the selected Ontario credit.
Confirm for the labour-based or cost-of-production route selected.
routes.apply: Do not treat the federal 10% benchmark as a universal provincial ceiling.

routes.regions: Québec: Montréal, Québec City and regional Québec
routes.allowance: 0% for a non-Québec-resident producer's remuneration under the relevant producer provision.
routes.apply: Qualifying producer remuneration requires the individual to be Québec resident when providing the services. No separate fixed percentage verified for eligible resident fees.

routes.regions: Alberta: Calgary, Edmonton and regional Alberta
routes.allowance: 10% of actual B+C is a general reasonableness reference, rather than an absolute maximum.
routes.apply: Higher fees require support.

routes.allowance: Producer fees normally 10% of B+C; 15% for qualifying documentaries below C$2.5 million.
routes.apply: Corporate overhead has its own corresponding allowance. Exceptions are discretionary.

routes.regions: Nova Scotia: Halifax and regional areas
routes.allowance: Eligible compensation is limited by C$150,000 of incentive per individual, not C$150,000 of fee.
routes.apply: Thus the fee ceiling is C$150,000 ÷ applicable incentive rate: at 25%, C$600,000. Resident-labour and additional-role restrictions also apply.

routes.allowance: Confirm separately for the labour-based and all-spend routes.
routes.apply: No reliable producer-specific numerical ceiling established in this review.

routes.allowance: Combined producer fees and corporate overhead: 30% of B+C for budgets up to C$500,000; above that, 20% of B+C, capped at C$2 million, under the published business guidelines.
routes.apply: Treaty co-productions use the Canadian share.

routes.allowance: Confirm the approved territorial rebate cost schedule.
routes.apply: No numerical producer-fee maximum verified.

routes.allowance: Confirm the approved Nunavut-spend allocation.
routes.apply: Producer residency, ownership, control and reasonable remuneration are reviewed; no universal percentage verified.

routes.regions: California: Los Angeles and outside the zone
routes.allowance: 0% for ATL producer/EP fees.
routes.apply: Limited qualifying BTL work by someone also credited as a producer is a separate exception, capped at $100,000 for the specified roles.

routes.allowance: Fees for no more than two producers, within a shared ATL pool of 40% of all other qualified production costs.
routes.apply: This is not 40% of the total budget.

routes.regions: New Jersey: inside and outside the 30-mile zone
routes.allowance: General route: $750,000 per individual.
routes.apply: Studio/film-lease routes have additional ATL allowances. Certain qualifying partner productions can also include apportioned out-of-state producer fees within a 7.5% pool shared with rights fees and production insurance.

routes.allowance: $500,000 per person for W-2 compensation.
routes.apply: The same salary ceiling does not apply to qualifying loan-out/other eligible payment arrangements; Georgia work and tax requirements still apply.

routes.allowance: Shared ATL ceiling of 40% of Louisiana expenditure.
routes.apply: The former $3 million individual compensation limit was removed for the applicable post-July 2025 regime.

routes.allowance: $500,000 per individual, also constrained by 40% of Illinois production spending for all ATL, and 12% for related-party ATL in aggregate.
routes.apply: Limited exceptions exist to the 40% rule.

routes.allowance: Published programme guidance: $1 million total compensation per Texas-resident worker per project.
routes.apply: Non-resident producer wages do not qualify under that resident-payroll provision.

routes.allowance: First $1 million per individual; excess compensation is excluded.
Payroll provision excludes an employee's salary where it is $1 million or more.
routes.apply: This is an exclusion threshold, not simply a rebate on the first $1 million.

routes.allowance: Producer fees share the 25% ATL ceiling on statutory qualifying production expenditure.
routes.apply: Relevant Oklahoma taxpayer/loan-out requirements apply.

routes.allowance: First $1 million per ATL employee, resident or non-resident, subject to qualifying Kentucky services.
OPIF rules exclude compensation paid to an individual receiving more than $1 million.
routes.apply: Treat this as a potential whole-payment exclusion, not merely a cap on the excess.

routes.allowance: 0% for non-resident ATL producers.
routes.apply: Resident qualifying wages can be considered; no separate producer percentage established.

routes.allowance: Producer fees up to 10% of total Puerto Rico production expenditure, restricted to Puerto Rico-resident producers, with payment and tax evidence.
Route-dependent.
routes.apply: The payroll-credit exclusion for compensation of $1 million or more must be distinguished from the production-expense credit, which can have different treatment. Confirm before assigning a maximum.

routes.allowance: Do not assume a currently available award: the state has paused new certification applications and says the first available credit is in 2031.
routes.apply: Existing certifications need separate review.

routes.allowance: Confirm resident/non-resident status and ordinary versus Film Partner treatment.
routes.apply: No single current maximum verified for both routes.

routes.allowance: Confirm producer-specific treatment.
routes.apply: The commonly quoted principal-cast ceiling should not be used as a producer-fee allowance.

routes.allowance: Confirm current individual compensation treatment in the approved incentive agreement.
routes.apply: No current numerical maximum verified.

routes.allowance: Confirm the approved qualifying compensation and fee allocation.
routes.apply: No producer-specific percentage verified.

routes.allowance: Confirm qualifying Ohio services and fee classification.
routes.apply: No producer-specific percentage verified.

routes.allowance: Confirm qualifying Arizona production labour and fee classification.
routes.apply: No producer-specific percentage verified.

routes.allowance: Confirm qualifying producer compensation.
routes.apply: Different island incentive rates do not themselves establish a different producer-fee allowance.
